title: Wrong sideman credit and tunes taken by others
summary: A record lists a cornetist she never knew; she says others recorded her tunes and nothing could be done about it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Ms. Wallace, in November 1926, around -- in 1926, I see that they say here that there was a Cicero Thomas who played the coronet. And somebody else wrote underneath it that you never knew somebody by that name.
I wonder why they made a mistake like that and put a name down like Cicero Thomas for coronet in those tunes. It was "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman" and --
about somebody singing "I'm a Mighty Tight Woman." He said, somebody's singing your tune.
Oh, it was somebody else singing, then?
He said, somebody's singing your tune. And somebody just recorded my tune (unintelligible).
No, this was what the man told me when I was (unintelligible).
Oh, I get it. Isn't that funny.
What they would do, they would take your music and there was nothing you could do about it. Nothing you could do about it.
And you never did know such a man?
No. They take your music and go on singing it. Now I sing, but you know, sometimes (unintelligible).
